name: What Dependency Injection Solves
overview: A service that builds its own database client brings the database to every test. Give it a replaceable dependency and see what gets easier.

sections.title: Spot the hard-coded dependency
sections.content: If a service creates its own database client, changing that client can mean editing the service. Its unit tests may also need infrastructure they were never meant to exercise.

images.caption: Constructor injection lets the same service use a real dependency or a test double.

sections.title: Move the choice outside
sections.content: Accept the collaborator as a constructor parameter. Let application configuration choose the real implementation and let tests provide a fake.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.content: Test the same business behavior with a fake. Keep an integration test for real wiring. Measure the setup effort before declaring victory.

keyPoints: Refactor one hard-coded dependency and swap in a test double. You've succeeded when the business code works with either implementation.

interviewQA.question: What is the main gain from DI?
interviewQA.answer: A class can use a different collaborator without changing its business logic.

interviewQA.question: Does DI remove the need for integration tests?
interviewQA.answer: No. Unit tests can isolate behavior, and integration tests still verify real wiring and interactions.
